title: GAM4water: An R-based method for extracting wetted areas from remotely-sensed images
author: Redana, Lancaster, et al.

steps.title: Prepare and harmonize rasters
steps.instruction: Ensure each input raster has a reference CRS; optionally reproject all rasters to a chosen projection system; homogenize resolution using terra::resample, selecting either the lower‑resolution or higher‑resolution raster as the reference; optionally crop rasters to the AOI polygon shapefile; optionally degrade resolution with an aggregating factor (number of pixels in each horizontal and vertical direction) using terra::aggregate, which computes the mean of the grouped pixels.

steps.title: Stack rasters and extract pixel data
steps.instruction: Stack all input rasters into a single multilayer raster, then extract radiometric values for every pixel contained in the input shapefile (wet/dry samples) across each layer; store the extracted values together with pixel coordinates in a data frame where each row represents one annotated observation.

steps.title: Create training and validation sets
steps.instruction: Randomly divide the data frame into a training set and a validation set, ensuring that each set contains a 2/3 ratio of wetted to dry pixels.

steps.title: Fit default GAM classification model
steps.instruction: Choose whether to include pixel position (x, y) in the model (Eq. 1 uses position, Eq. 2 does not); select the desired model form; fit the model with mgcv::bam using a thin‑plate spline shrinkage smoother for f1 and a tensor‑product smoother for f2, estimating smoothing parameters via fast Restricted Maximum Likelihood (fREML); optionally specify the number of processor cores for parallel execution; optionally output a model summary and predictor‑effects plot.

steps.title: Classify AOI pixels
steps.instruction: Apply the fitted GAM to every pixel in the AOI to obtain wet‑probability values; classify a pixel as dry if its probability ≤ 0.5 and as wet if > 0.5 (the threshold can be changed by the user).
